questions.question: Explain the major stages in the development of the modern sports industry. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the major stages in the development of the modern sports industry.
  • Indicative answer: The modern sports industry developed through several broad stages. Initially,
  • sports were largely community-based recreational and competitive activities. The development of
  • organized clubs, associations and formal competitions introduced structured management and
  • governance. The expansion of professional sports created paid athletes, commercial competitions and
  • sponsorship opportunities. Television and other broadcasting technologies expanded audiences and
  • generated media revenue. In the digital era, social media, streaming services, data analytics and
  • online ticketing have transformed fan engagement and commercial operations.

questions.question: Explain the concept of dynamic pricing in sports ticketing and identify the factors that can influence ticket prices. / [CO3] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the concept of dynamic pricing in sports ticketing and identify the factors that can
  • influence ticket prices.
  • Dynamic pricing is a ticketing strategy in which ticket prices change according to demand,
  • availability and market conditions. Prices may increase when demand is high and decrease when
  • demand is low. Factors include team popularity, match importance, opponent strength, venue
  • capacity, seating category, time remaining before the event and current ticket sales. Organizations use
  • dynamic pricing to manage demand and maximise revenue while considering transparency and fan
  • affordability.

questions.solution_html:
Comprehensive Evaluation Rubric (Essay / Long Problem):
• Introduction & Conceptual Foundation (2 Marks): Comprehensive overview, definitions, contextual scope, and historical/theoretical relevance.
• Detailed Structural Analysis & Derivations (5 Marks): Deep exploration covering all relevant dimensions, mathematical proofs, architectural diagrams, or comparative taxonomies.
• Practical Applications & Critical Evaluation (2 Marks): Real-world applications, computational complexity, empirical validation, or critical critique.
• Conclusion & Summary (1 Mark): Concise synthesis connecting theoretical outcomes with course objectives.
Valuation Guidance: Full marks are awarded for clear structural organization, labeled diagrams/formulations where applicable, and exhaustive coverage of all sub-parts.
